title: Death of suspect in Hamilton poilice custody ruled an accident
article: A coroner's jury has ruled that the death of a 26-year-old transsexual and intravenous drug user while in the custody of Hamilton police was accidental.
The jury found that Abdirhman Ali Abdi, who was known on the streets of Hamilton by the female identity Chevranna, died after choking on vomit brought on by cocaine poisoning.
The jury did not make any recommendations aimed at preventing another death in similar circumstances.
Abdi went into cardiac arrest on February 20th, 2003, about 10 minutes after running from an eighth-floor apartment screaming about being chased by dogs and bikers.
Police arrested Abdi and carried her down seven floors of stairs because elevators were out of order, and once in the lobby, they discovered she was not breathing and had no pulse.
Hamilton police lawyer Marco Visentini argued that although Abdi resisted arrest, there was no evidence of excessive force.
